answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a time-locked stake whose cost rises with the number of identities one operator controls: the first bond is small, the tenth costs ten times more, so mass-producing fake agents grows exponentially expensive. Like a vine climbing toward a summit, reputation only grows through verified work, while a fresh identity starts in a cold tundra with no trust, no history and no access to high-value jobs until independent peers attest it. Attackers must pay real capital and time for every fake, while honest agents build standing cheaply.
